name: Cen Zhaoxiong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Times China Holdings (HKEX: 1233), Guangzhou
profile: Cen Zhaoxiong (岑钊雄, known in Hong Kong filings as Shum Chiu Hung) founded Guangzhou property developer Times China (formerly Times Property) and has chaired it since its 2008 Hong Kong listing. He remains chairman/CEO while the developer works through a debt restructuring; he is also an NPC deputy for Guangdong.
interesting_fact: He is a member of China's National People's Congress for Guangdong and President of the Guangdong Youth Entrepreneurs Association; he was named a 'Guangzhou Model Philanthropist' in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: His company co-founded the Guangdong Times Museum in 2003 with the Guangdong Museum of Art, and later commissioned Rem Koolhaas and Alain Fouraux to design its permanent space on top of a Times residential tower (opened 2010).
notes: Forbes 'Cen Zhaoxiong' = Mandarin pinyin of 岑钊雄; HKEX/company English name is Shum Chiu Hung. Times China is in debt restructuring; avoid the topic. No personal social accounts found; route via IR.

name: Mary Alice Malone Jr
current_role: Founder & creative director, Malone Souliers; owner of Duo Boots; director, The Campbell's Company (since July 2025)
profile: Great-granddaughter of Campbell's Soup inventor John T. Dorrance; she and her sister inherited a combined ~18% Campbell's stake when their mother died in June 2025, and she took her mother's board seat. London-based, she trained as a shoemaker, founded luxury footwear label Malone Souliers in 2014 and revived UK brand Duo Boots in 2020.
interesting_fact: An accomplished dressage rider who grew up on her mother's horse-breeding farm in Coatesville, Pa., she once made the U.S. Junior Olympic Equestrian Team before turning to shoemaking.
deep_cut_fact: She trained at the Cordwainers shoemaking school in East London; her signature 'Maureen' heel (SS2015) was initially a hard sell to buyers ('Trying to get people to buy Maureen took a bit of convincing, at first') but became a bestseller.
notes: Recently inherited; mother died June 2025 (avoid condolence-heavy openers unless appropriate). Best route is Malone Souliers press. Instagram is the brand account, not personal.

name: Li Zhixiong
current_role: Director, Shenzhen Longsys Electronics (江波龙, SZSE ChiNext: 301308)
profile: Li Zhixiong (李志雄) is a long-time director and major shareholder of Shenzhen Longsys Electronics, a memory and storage maker he joined in 2004 after research stints. Longsys bought the Lexar brand from Micron in 2017 and listed on ChiNext in 2022; Li still held ~3.9% after share sales completed in June 2026.
interesting_fact: Lexar, the U.S. consumer storage brand Longsys acquired from Micron in 2017, became a global partner of the Argentina national football team.
notes: Low public profile; not the CEO (Chairman/CEO is Cai Huabo). Holding reduced to 3.9% per June 2026 filing (stockstar/10jqka). Best route: Longsys marketing/IR.

name: Zhang Changhong
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (~33%), Shanghai DZH (formerly Great Wisdom, SSE: 601519); no longer chairman since 2016
profile: Zhang Changhong (张长虹, b. 1958, Chengdu) founded Shanghai DZH in 2000, building it into a leading Chinese provider of real-time market data and trading software that competes with Reuters and Bloomberg; it listed in Shanghai in 2011. He stepped down as chairman in 2016 but remains the controlling shareholder as DZH is merged into Xiangcai Co. via share swap.
interesting_fact: In the early 2000s he proposed a 'full circulation' plan to resolve China's split-share structure, letting non-tradable state and corporate shares gradually gain trading rights.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, he earned a master's degree in philosophy at Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi'an (1987) and taught at Nanjing Aeronautical School, a forerunner of Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics.
notes: Sensitive: CSRC fined him and banned him from securities markets in 2016 over DZH's 2013 accounts; detained in 2019 per Beijing News. Current DZH chairman/GM is Zhang Zhihong. Probably a poor podcast fit; only route is company IR.

name: Christian Herz
current_role: Managing director and ~45% owner, Mayfair Vermögensverwaltung SE (Herz family office), Hamburg
profile: Grandson of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz and son of Günter Herz, who ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. After Günter and his sister Daniela were bought out of Tchibo in 2003 they built Hamburg family office Mayfair, whose investments have included Puma and DNV GL; Christian owns about 45% and helps steer investment decisions as a managing director.
interesting_fact: Mayfair was once a major Puma shareholder, selling its stake into PPR's 2007 takeover offer, and held 36.5% of ship-classification group DNV GL until selling back to the Det Norske Veritas Foundation in December 2017.
notes: Very private; no interviews, website or social accounts found for him or Mayfair. Avoid the Herz family disputes and Vapiano. Route would be via the family office's registered Hamburg office (no published email found).

name: Yahaya Ahmad
profile: Tan Sri Yahaya Ahmad, founder, chairman and CEO of Malaysia's DRB-HICOM group (owner of national carmaker Proton; nicknamed the 'Car Czar'), appeared on the 1996 Forbes list. He died with his wife in a helicopter crash near Kuala Lipis, Pahang, on 3 March 1997.
notes: Deceased 1997. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahaya_Ahmad. Matched via Forbes 1996 Malaysian listing; no current outreach target.

name: Lin Yu-Chia
current_role: Deceased (reported to have died aged 100); founder of Taiwan Glass Industry Corp.
profile: Lin Yu-Chia (林玉嘉) founded Taiwan Glass Industry Corp. (台玻) in 1964 and handed control to sons Lin Pei-Feng (chairman) and Lin Pei-Shih in 2009. He was on Hurun lists in 2014-2015; an investor-community profile reports he died aged 100 (exact date not found).
notes: Death source is a non-news CMoney note (https://www.cmoney.tw/notes/note-detail.aspx?nid=173744); consistent with reports he turned 87 around 2002 (Business Today). Taiwan Glass is now run by son Lin Pei-Feng; not an outreach target.

name: Paul Sciarra
profile: New Jersey-born Yale graduate and former Radius Ventures VC who co-founded Pinterest (via Cold Brew Labs) with Ben Silbermann, serving as its early president/CEO before leaving in 2012; he still holds roughly 5% of Pinterest. Since 2014 he has been executive chairman of electric air-taxi maker Joby Aviation, where he owns about 6%.
interesting_fact: He and his wife Jennifer signed the Giving Pledge in 2019, promising to give away at least half their wealth.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Pinterest he was an entrepreneur-in-residence at Andreessen Horowitz, and in 2014 he made Joby Aviation's first outside investment, becoming executive chairman of what was then a small Santa Cruz-area aircraft startup.
notes: Low-key, rarely interviewed. Strong fit for an energy/electric-aviation episode; route via Joby press team.

name: André Kasprzak
current_role: Co-owner and member of the Board of Directors, ECCO Sko A/S (Denmark)
profile: Third-generation co-owner of Danish shoemaker ECCO, founded in 1963 by his grandfather Karl Toosbuy; he owns the company with his mother Hanni and sister Anna. He joined ECCO's supervisory board in 2017 after his father Dieter stepped down as CEO, bringing e-commerce and digital experience.
interesting_fact: Before joining the board he served in the Danish military and played professional golf on the Nordic League (ECCO also makes a well-known golf shoe line).
deep_cut_fact: In early 2015 he worked at Scandinavian online fashion retailer Boozt, then helped build a new European e-commerce platform at KRM AG, ECCO's European retail arm; on joining the board he said 'ECCO has always been an essential part of my life.'
notes: Private family-owned company; route via ECCO group press office. Mother Hanni Toosbuy Kasprzak has been chair.

name: Jean Madar
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Inter Parfums, Inc. (Nasdaq: IPAR), New York
profile: Jean Madar co-founded fragrance licensor Interparfums with ESSEC classmate Philippe Benacin after learning about the industry's high margins in business school; it listed on Nasdaq in 1988 at a ~$4M valuation and is now worth billions. As CEO since 1997 he runs the U.S. operations (brands such as Montblanc, Coach, Jimmy Choo licences sit across the group).
interesting_fact: Madar never wears fragrance himself, to keep his sense of smell clear.
deep_cut_fact: The company's original name, Jean Philippe Fragrances, was a contraction of the founders' first names, Jean and Philippe, and it started out selling inexpensive alternatives to pricier designer scents before moving upmarket.

public_contacts.value: dsullivan@theequitygroup.com (Devin Sullivan, The Equity Group - IR agency)

notes: Accessible public-company CEO who does investor calls; IR agency The Equity Group is the published route.

name: Lau Ngai Leung
current_role: Chairman, Chong Sai Enterprise Group (澳門創世企業集團), Macau; Macau deputy to China's National People's Congress
profile: Lau Ngai Leung (劉藝良; Portuguese romanisation Lao Ngai Leong) is a Macau real-estate businessman who chairs Chong Sai Enterprise Group and was ranked Macau's richest person on the 2021 Hurun China list. A five-term Macau NPC deputy and former Executive Council member, he is also a vice-chairman of the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese.
interesting_fact: He received an honorary Doctor of Social Sciences from the University of Macau in 2018 and is an 'Honorary Citizen of Chaozhou'.
deep_cut_fact: As an NPC deputy he pushed for the Standing Committee decision that let Macau exercise jurisdiction over the University of Macau's new Hengqin campus, and for longer Zhuhai-Macau border checkpoint hours.
notes: Search under 'Lao Ngai Leong' (Macau spelling). Politically prominent; no company website or published contact found. Latest-status confirmation for 2025-26 not found.

name: Jiang Yehua
current_role: Chairman (per Forbes), Chongqing Huayu Group (重庆华宇集团), Chongqing
profile: Jiang Yehua (蒋业华) built Chongqing Huayu Group into one of the largest real estate developers in Chongqing, with businesses spanning property development and property management. Business-registry listings now show Jiang Jie as the group's legal representative, suggesting day-to-day control may have passed on.
interesting_fact: He worked as a construction worker before setting up his own business.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews, official site or published contact verified. Registry (via jobui.com/cnpp.cn) lists Jiang Jie as legal representative of 重庆华宇集团有限公司; current role of Jiang Yehua unconfirmed.

name: Mohammed Al Fahim
current_role: Chairman, Makarem General Trading & Real Estate LLC; supervisory board member, Al Fahim Group, Abu Dhabi (as of 2019)
profile: Most likely Mohammed Abdul Jalil Al Fahim (b. 1948, Al Ain), who joined his family's Abu Dhabi business in 1968 after studying in England and diversified it from car imports into real estate, hotels and industry. He later chaired the Al Fahim family council and Makarem, and is best known as author of the bestselling memoir 'From Rags to Riches: A Story of Abu Dhabi' (1995).
interesting_fact: His 1995 memoir of pre-oil Abu Dhabi has been translated into about ten languages and was adapted into a short film, 'The Early Years: The Untold Story of Abu Dhabi'.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in the Ruler's palace in Al Ain going barefoot with friends, started at a Qur'an school and joined Al Falahiya School in 1959; he founded two special-needs centres in Abu Dhabi and keeps a private museum of documents on old Abu Dhabi.
notes: Input only says Forbes 1999 UAE list with no company; match to the Al Fahim Group/author is probable, not confirmed. Latest coverage found is 2019; current status unverified. A relative, Mohamed Abdullah Al Fahim, also works in the group, so check name carefully.

name: Martha Stewart
current_role: Founder of the Martha Stewart brand (owned by Marquee Brands since 2019), media personality and author
profile: Martha Stewart turned a 1970s Westport, Connecticut catering business into Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, the publishing, TV and merchandising empire that made her a billionaire on paper when it went public in 1999. The brand is now owned by Marquee Brands; she remains its face, with 100 books (Martha: The Cookbook, 2024), a 2024 Netflix documentary and NBC's 'Yes, Chef!' with José Andrés (2025).
interesting_fact: In 2023, at 81, she became the oldest woman ever to appear on the cover of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue.
deep_cut_fact: As a 10-year-old in Nutley, N.J., she babysat for New York Yankees Mickey Mantle, Yogi Berra and Gil McDougald and organised birthday parties for Mantle's four sons; she later worked as a Wall Street stockbroker from 1967 before starting her catering business.
notes: Forbes billionaire only in 2005; current net worth estimated far lower. Avoid 2004 conviction. Very accessible publicly but heavily agented; Marquee Brands (marqueebrands.com) handles brand partnerships. Her blog themarthablog.com is personal and frequently updated.

name: Raj Menda
profile: Raj Menda co-founded Bengaluru-based RMZ Corp with his family in the early 2000s and built it into one of India's largest developers and owners of Grade-A office parks, later selling large portfolios to Brookfield. Wholly family-owned, RMZ now spans real estate, infrastructure, private capital and RMZ Digital Infrastructure (data centres); Raj co-chairs its supervisory board with brother Manoj.
interesting_fact: He is a former chairman of YPO India and a past president of CREDAI (Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India).
deep_cut_fact: He was the first Indian to chair the jury of the Urban Land Institute's global Awards for Excellence.

public_contacts.value: akash.philip@rmz.com (Head of PR, RMZ - published media contact)

notes: Good data-center angle via RMZ Digital Infrastructure (MD Ryan D'Souza). Next-gen (Sidharth, Mihir Menda) now run day-to-day and give interviews; route via RMZ Head of PR.

name: Shen Tianqing
current_role: Founder of Jiayuan Group (佳源集团), Jiaxing, Zhejiang; former chairman of HK-listed Jiayuan International Group
profile: Shen Tianqing (沈天晴, also known as Shen Yuxing) founded Zhejiang property developer Jiayuan Group and chaired Hong Kong-listed Jiayuan International from its 2016 listing, injecting most of his private property assets into it. The group defaulted from 2022 and Jiayuan International was ordered wound up.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: his listed company is in liquidation, bonds defaulted, and Huxiu (July 2026) reports HKEX issued a director-unsuitability statement against him in Jan 2026 (https://www.huxiu.com/article/4877161.html). No contacts recorded.

name: Chan Hung Ming
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director and controlling shareholder, Grand Ming Group Holdings (HKEX: 1271)
profile: Chan Hung Ming (陳孔明) co-founded Hong Kong contractor-developer Grand Ming Group, which he has helped manage since 1995, with 40+ years in construction and property. He pivoted the group into data centres, building the iTech Towers in Tsuen Wan, Kwai Chung and Fanling; in 2025 the group was reported to be negotiating sales of its data-centre assets to Bain Capital and then Actis.
interesting_fact: Grand Ming's iTech Tower 2 in Kwai Chung is a 15-storey purpose-built data centre of about 100,000 sq ft for up to 1,400 racks and 6 MW of critical power.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as a builder, he holds a Higher Certificate in Building Technology from the Hong Kong Polytechnic; Grand Ming's first data centre, iTech Tower 1 in Tsuen Wan, was converted from an industrial building around 2007, years before Hong Kong's data-centre boom.
notes: Strong data-center fit. Group reported losses and covenant waivers in 2025 and was selling data-centre assets (Actis deal reported Oct 2025, completion unconfirmed) - avoid financial-distress framing.

name: Neeraj Kochhar
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Viraj Profiles Ltd (stainless steel), Mumbai/Tarapur
profile: Neeraj Raja Kochhar moved from a logistics business into stainless steel in 1992 and built Viraj Profiles, a privately held maker of stainless long products (wire rods, wire, bars, profiles, flanges, fasteners) based at Tarapur, Maharashtra, with reported turnover near $1.5bn. He entered Hurun's global rich list in 2025.
interesting_fact: Viraj began in 1991 with a single induction furnace and about 150 employees; its melting capacity has since been reported at over 600,000 tonnes a year.
deep_cut_fact: Before stainless steel he ran a logistics business; in 2019 he pushed Viraj toward 'green' production using recycled scrap and automatic temperature control, saying 'Being eco-friendly is one of the top priorities of our company.'
notes: Input lacks country; he is Indian (Mumbai). Email on viraj.com is Cloudflare-obfuscated (decoded as corpcomm@). Possible energy-intensive-industry/decarbonisation angle.
